channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Soraya Thronicke troca o Podemos pelo PSB e buscará a reeleição ao Senado
item.description: Senator Soraya Thronicke left Podemos and joined the PSB to run for Senate re-election in 2026. She had previously run for president in 2022 under União Brasil, receiving 0.51% of the vote, and will now team up with federal deputy Vander Loubet (PT) in Mato Grosso do Sul. The party switch occurred on the eve of the partisan window closure, with endorsement from Vice President Geraldo Alckmin.

item.title: Defesa de Bolsonaro apresenta ao STF queixa-crime contra André Janones por calúnia e difamação
item.description: The defense of former President Jair Bolsonaro filed a criminal complaint at the STF against Deputy André Janones for slander and defamation, claiming he called Bolsonaro a 'thief' and 'bum' in a widely viewed video. Lawyers argue that Bolsonaro, barred from using social media due to his conviction for attempted coup, cannot publicly defend himself, creating an unequal situation that violates the constitutional principle of contradiction.

item.title: MEC disponibiliza aplicativo gratuito com oito mil livros
item.description: The Ministry of Education launched the free MEC Livros app, offering nearly eight thousand literary works for reading, including copyrighted books, public domain titles, and features like personalization, AI, and notifications. The app is available on Android, computers, and integrates with gov.br, with plans to release MEC Idiomas for English and Spanish language learning.

item.title: Aneel retoma processo e pode recomendar cassação do contrato da Enel em São Paulo
item.description: Aneel will vote on Tuesday on whether to open a supervisory process that could lead to a recommendation to cancel Enel's electricity distribution contract in São Paulo due to repeated power outages, including the December blackout affecting over 2 million properties and causing estimated losses of R$1.54 billion. The final decision rests with the Ministry of Mines and Energy, while São Paulo's mayor Ricardo Nunes and governor Tarcísio de Freitas publicly support contract termination, which would entail a billion-real compensation to Enel if enacted.

item.title: Governo indica Guilherme Mello para presidência de Conselho de Administração da Petrobras
item.description: The Lula government has nominated Guilherme Mello, Secretary of Economic Policy at the Ministry of Finance, to preside over Petrobras' Board of Directors, replacing Bruno Moretti, who was appointed Minister of Planning and Budget. Mello had previously been advocated by former minister Fernando Haddad for a position on the Central Bank's board, but his move to Petrobras makes a Central Bank appointment less likely. The market reacted negatively to the potential Central Bank nomination, citing concerns over Mello's academic background and PT ties, fearing increased tolerance for inflation.

item.title: Crise durante janela partidária deve impor DR decisiva entre União e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The crisis during the party window between União Brasil and PL, driven by PL's offensive against União Brasil's ranks, has led party leaders to believe the situation may force Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to seek dialogue to secure the party's support for his presidential bid. Despite tensions, União Brasil executives acknowledge that a conciliatory stance by Flávio could help gain the party's backing, though Lula-supporting members push for the party to remain neutral in the national election.

item.title: As perspectivas de Cláudio Castro para viabilizar candidatura ao Senado
item.description: Claudio Castro, former governor of Rio de Janeiro, faces significant hurdles in running for the Senate due to ineligibility imposed by the TSE until 2030 for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 elections. Although the PL officially supports him, historical STF rulings show that appeals against TSE decisions are rarely admitted or reformed, making his taking office uncertain even if elected.

item.title: Lindbergh pede ao STF prisão de Eduardo Bolsonaro após fala sobre eleições
item.description: Federal Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) has asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to order the preventive detention of former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro following the latter's statements alleging fraud in the 2022 elections. Lindbergh argues that Eduardo’s remarks may constitute incitement to disobey the law and threaten democratic order, also requesting alternative precautionary measures if preventive arrest is deemed inappropriate. The request comes amid rising political tensions surrounding the 2026 elections and the legitimacy of the 2022 electoral outcome.

item.title: Lula sanciona a criação de 474 cargos efetivos na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.374/26, creating 474 effective positions in the Electoral Justice (232 judicial analysts and 242 judicial technicians), plus 75 commissioned positions and 245 commissioned functions, with an estimated annual budget impact of R$ 109.4 million. The resources will address growth in the electorate, candidacies, and judicial proceedings, strengthening electronic voting security, combating fake news, and ensuring compliance with CNJ guidelines. The measure originated from TSE’s Bill 4/24 and requires budgetary authorization to take financial effect.

item.title: Nova lei reajusta em 8% salário de funcionários do Ministério Público e do Conselho do Ministério Público
item.description: Law 15.373/26, signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, establishes an 8% salary increase for effective, commissioned, and commissioned functions employees of the Union’s Public Ministry and the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP), effective July 1, 2026. Lula vetoed extending the increase to 2027 and 2028, stating it would raise personnel spending for the next government, which would be unconstitutional. The bill’s rapporteur in the Chamber, Deputy Isnaldo Bulhões Jr. (MDB-AL), said the adjustment respects the constitutional cap and maintains symmetry with judiciary and CNJ employees.

item.title: As duas novas pesquisas de intenção de voto para presidente
item.description: Two new presidential election polls for 2026 will be released this week: Ideia on Wednesday the 8th (based on 1,500 interviews with a 2.5-point margin of error) and Datafolha on Saturday the 11th (based on 2,004 interviews with a 2-point margin of error). Both institutes had previously shown a technical tie in a potential runoff between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in March, with Lula narrowly ahead in both surveys. These are the first polls since Ronaldo Caiado was confirmed as the PSD’s pre-candidate.

item.title: Tarcísio pedala ao som de “Cocoricó” e minimiza cansaço
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas rode a bicycle on a recently reopened bike path while listening to the opening theme of the cartoon Cocoricó, downplaying fatigue with the remark "you're not tired, you just haven't chosen the right music". The 2 km stretch of the Franco Montoro Bike Path, blocked since 2014 due to construction of the Line 17-Gold monorail, was reopened on March 31, 2026, alongside the inauguration of the line connecting the southern zone to Congonhas Airport. Tarcísio criticized the delay as a "disrespect" that hinders many people's lives.

item.title: PT anuncia filiação de Kátia Abreu: ‘gesto de maturidade política’
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) in Tocantins announced the affiliation of former Minister and Senator Kátia Abreu to the party, in an event held in Palmas with the presence of state leaders and support from President Lula. Kátia emphasized that her joining aims to strengthen the PT's grassroots in the state and support Lula's 2026 re-election, overcoming past differences in a gesture of political maturity.

item.title: Cid Gomes e Capitão Wagner lideram disputa ao Senado no Ceará
item.description: Senator Cid Gomes (PSB) and former federal deputy Capitão Wagner (União Brasil) are technically tied in the lead for the two Senate seats in Ceará, with 47.0% and 46.3% voting intentions, respectively, according to a Futura/Apex poll released on April 6, 2026. The survey, conducted from March 30 to April 1 with 1,000 respondents, has a 95% confidence level and a 3.1 percentage point margin of error.

item.title: O evento mais importante de Zema em abril
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and 2026 presidential candidate, will hold his most important campaign event in April on the 16th in São Paulo. Titled 'Enough of rich government and poor people,' the event will present a synthesis of his government program. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Lula tem 56,1% contra 36,2% de Flávio entre eleitores do Ceará
item.description: A poll conducted by Instituto Futura/Apex and released on April 6, 2026 shows that, in a potential second round for the presidency in Ceará, Lula (PT) leads with 56.1% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 36.2%. Blank, null, and undecided voters account for 7.6%. The survey also measured rejection: Flávio Bolsonaro is the most rejected candidate (53.3%), followed by Lula (36.7%).

item.title: Da Amazônia ao centro do debate: como Cileide Moussallem amplia sua influência no cenário nacional
item.description: Cileide Moussallem expanded her national influence from the Amazon, leveraging digital media and firm positioning to build authority without relying on traditional power structures. Her rise reflects broader structural changes in Brazil: increased connectivity in the North, fragmented news consumption, and the growing political relevance of the female electorate, which now constitutes a majority of voters.

item.title: De ministros do STF a Neymar: os próximos testes de popularidade do Datafolha
item.description: The upcoming Datafolha poll, conducted from Tuesday to Thursday this week, will gather opinion data on topics beyond the 2026 elections, including individual evaluations of STF ministers, public indebtedness, and Neymar’s potential call-up for the World Cup. For the first time, the poll will list Ronaldo Caiado as the sole PSD presidential candidate following withdrawals by Ratinho Júnior and Eduardo Leite, and will include Cabo Daciolo as a new Mobiliza pre-candidate. Results may be published starting Saturday, the 11th, pending Folha de S. Paulo’s final decision.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: na avalanches de pesquisas, entenda o que mais importa sobre a disputa
item.description: The abundance of electoral polls reveals a polarized and stable race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro, with narrow margins and neither candidate achieving a comfortable lead. The convergence of results across different polling institutes lends scientific consistency to the scenario, indicating a relatively consolidated electoral landscape at this early stage. Alternative candidacies fail to break the dominant polarization, limiting their competitiveness.

item.title: STF condena a 14 anos de prisão empresários que financiaram ida de bolsonaristas ao atos do 8 de Janeiro
item.description: The STF sentenced three businessmen to 14 years in prison for financing transportation of Bolsonaro supporters to the January 8, 2023, anti-democratic acts, characterizing their actions as 'subjective adherence' to a democratic rupture. Donations ranged from R$500 to R$10,000, and the defendants were also linked to other anti-democratic activities following the 2022 elections.

item.title: Quanto Lula pega no supino?
item.description: First Lady Janja shared a video on social media showing President Lula working out at the gym, highlighting his physical condition despite his age. The post was published on May 6 and sparked discussions about the president’s public image and the government’s political communication strategy.

item.title: Pesquisa aponta que maioria dos deputados não se aprofundou em PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: A survey shows that most Brazilian deputies have not deeply studied the PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work scale, despite claiming familiarity with the topic. 70% have not received impact assessments and 65% say financial effects were not measured, raising concerns about costs, inflation, informality, and small business closures. Despite political divergence, 69% believe the proposal will pass and 82% support voting before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Bolsonaro aciona STF contra Janones após ser chamado de "ladrão"
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro (PL) filed a lawsuit at the Supreme Federal Court (STF) against federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) over a video in which Janones called Bolsonaro a 'thief' and accused him of ordering the murders of former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and former Governor Geraldo Alckmin. Bolsonaro’s legal team claims the statements constitute defamation, slander, and insult, arguing he was denied the right to respond due to restrictions on his cell phone and social media use under house arrest, authorized by Justice Alexandre de Moraes. The defense seeks Janones’ conviction and compensation for moral damages.

item.title: “Um é o incendiário e o outro é o bombeiro”: a crise na família Bolsonaro que preocupa a direita
item.description: Public disputes within the Bolsonaro family reveal disorganization threatening Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential bid, with Eduardo Bolsonaro acting as an 'incendiary' and Flávio as a 'firefighter', according to political scientist Elias Tavares. The lack of coordination among allies and internal conflicts, including tensions with Michelle Bolsonaro, hinder right-wing unification, although Jair Bolsonaro remains the group’s key asset due to his vote-transfer capacity.

item.title: Governo Lula prepara pacote para dívidas e diesel a 6 meses da eleição
item.description: The Lula government is preparing a package of measures to ease household debt and reduce diesel prices six months ahead of the 2026 elections. The plan includes reviving the Desenrola Brasil debt renegotiation program, imposing possible caps on credit card revolving interest rates, and issuing a new provisional measure that could lower diesel prices by up to R$1.20 per liter through import subsidies, estimated to cost R$3 billion over two months.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Datafolha e Real Time Big Data divulgam pesquisas para presidente esta semana
item.description: Datafolha will release a new presidential voting intention poll between April 7 and 9, interviewing 2,004 voters nationwide. Registered with the TSE under BR-03770/2026, the results are expected to be published on Saturday, April 11. The survey is conducted in partnership with Real Time Big Data.

item.title: STF condena a 14 anos de prisão empresário que doou R$ 500 para levar manifestante ao 8 de janeiro
item.description: On June 4, 2026, the First Chamber of Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court (STF) sentenced businessman Alcides Hahn from Santa Catarina to 14 years in prison for financing R$500 to transport a participant to the January 8, 2023, coup attempt in Brasília. The court ruled his contribution facilitated actions that threatened democratic order.

item.title: Silvye Alves desiste de sair do União após alegar ‘coação’ em votação
item.description: Federal Deputy Silvye Alves (GO) announced she will remain in the União Brasil party after previously stating she would leave due to alleged 'coercion' to vote in favor of the Immunity PEC. She said she was pressured by 'influential people in the National Congress' to change her vote during the proposal's voting session, which she had initially opposed, and apologized to voters, calling her action 'cowardly'. The partisan window, open from March 5 to April 3, allowed party change without losing her mandate.

item.title: Crusoé: Janja posa de ‘tradwife’
item.description: Following Lula's electoral victory in 2022, Janja promised to redefine the role of First Lady. In a recent Instagram post, she shared a video preparing paca meat for her husband, with Lula arriving wearing a backward cap, sparking criticism for embracing 'tradwife' stereotypes. The content was first published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Caiado foca em SP e busca ‘voto envergonhado’ em Flávio para se firmar como opção a Lula
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) is focusing his pre-campaign on increasing national recognition, especially in São Paulo and in the digital environment, to position himself as a viable alternative to Lula and the PT. He aims to attract the 'shy vote' from the right that currently supports Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), arguing that his administrative experience and public trajectory make him a more solid and capable option. The strategy, led by pollster Paulo Vasconcellos, aims to show that Caiado is not merely a supporter of Flávio, but a candidate with real chances to win the 2026 election.

item.title: Janja faz live e mostra Lula malhando: “Sem IA e sem PowerPoint”
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva shared a video showing President Lula working out at a gym, stating he did 45 minutes on the treadmill followed by leg exercises, without AI or PowerPoint. The post is part of a Planalto strategy to emphasize the 80-year-old president’s vitality ahead of the 2026 elections, amid a 61% disapproval rating according to PoderData. The reference to 'PowerPoint' alludes to a recent GloboNews segment linking Lula to the Banco Master case, which the network later apologized for on air.

item.title: Lei determina que empresas divulguem campanhas de conscientização sobre vacinas, HPV e câncer
item.description: Law 15.377/26 amends the CLT to require companies to inform employees about official vaccination, HPV, and breast, cervical, and prostate cancer awareness campaigns, and grants workers up to 3 days of paid leave per year for preventive exams. Signed by President Lula and published in the Official Gazette, the law extends existing leave rights to include HPV screenings and mandates alignment with Ministry of Health guidelines.

item.title: A reviravolta na vida das vítimas do Césio 137 após repercussão de ‘Emergência Radioativa’
item.description: The Goiás government approved a pension increase for victims of the Goiânia Cs-137 accident following the global impact of the Netflix miniseries 'Emergência Radioativa'. Pensions for those directly exposed rose from R$1,908 to R$3,242, and for others from R$954 to R$1,621, benefiting 603 people. The adjustment, effective this month, fulfills a demand since 2018 after a 2023 veto citing lack of financial impact study.

item.title: Sancionada lei que reajusta salários de servidores da Defensoria Pública da União
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.372/26, which adjusts and restructures salaries for career and permanent positions in the Public Defender's Office of the Union (DPU), maintaining 20 salary levels for higher and intermediate positions. The law, originating from Bill PL 2004/24 approved by the Chamber in December 2025 and the Senate in March 2026, takes effect on July 1, 2026, with costs borne by the DPU. Rapporter Stélio Dener argued the 20-level model enables gradual progression, serving as an effective mechanism for talent retention and continuous qualification.

item.title: Lulinha voou em jato de advogado que doou R$ 2 milhões para Tarcísio
item.description: Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, son of Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, flew on a private jet owned by a lawyer based in São Paulo, Brasília, and Cuiabá. The lawyer reportedly donated R$ 2 million to the campaign of Tarcísio de Freitas, governor of São Paulo, according to documents obtained by Folha de S.Paulo. The incident raises concerns about potential influence conflicts involving relatives of public officials and political donors.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro transforma PEC do fim da reeleição em aceno para Tarcísio e centrão
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) advocated for a constitutional amendment to end presidential re-election as a strategy to gain support from governors and parties for his 2026 presidential bid. The proposal is seen as a political overture to the centrão and allies such as São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, amid a struggle for leadership within Brazil's right-wing.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: O novo capítulo da briga entre Eduardo e Nikolas
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program on Monday covered the feud between former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro and federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira, as well as Nunes Marques’ trip to Maceió on a flight funded by Banco Master’s lawyer. It also discussed the request to extend the Parliamentary Inquiry Commission (CPI).

item.title: Na briga entre Eduardo Bolsonaro e Nikolas Ferreira, torço pela briga
item.description: The text mocks the public feud between Eduardo Bolsonaro, who self-exiled to the U.S., and Nikolas Ferreira, a federal deputy from PL in Minas Gerais, suggesting the author enjoys watching the clash between two Bolsonarist allies. The conflict is portrayed as political entertainment, marked by exchanges of barbs and mutual accusations. The tone is sarcastic, highlighting the hypocrisy and theatrical nature of relationships within Brazil’s far-right.

item.title: Caiado, Flávio Bolsonaro e o 'preparo para governar'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado's campaign will emphasize his experience as governor, using the slogan 'ready to govern' to contrast with Flávio Bolsonaro, whom it portrays as less prepared. The tone is distinctly comparative, aiming to position Caiado as the most qualified candidate for office.

item.title: Filho de Jair Bolsonaro usa frase de Olavo de Carvalho para xingar Nikolas
item.description: Jair Renan Bolsonaro, councilman and youngest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, used a quote from Olavo de Carvalho to indirectly insult federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira as a 'whore', following an internal bolsonarist dispute involving his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro. The exchange of insults among Bolsonaro allies gained national attention, with figures such as Michelle Bolsonaro, Mario Frias, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro intervening to call for unity and end the public feuds. The episode highlights growing fragmentation and internal conflict within Brazil’s right-wing amid preparations for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Ministro André Mendonça desobriga Ibaneis de comparecer à CPI do Crime
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça ruled that former DF governor Ibaneis Rocha is not required to testify before the Crime CPI regarding negotiations for BRB’s attempted purchase of Banco Master, despite the commission’s March convocation. The decision also excuses him from speaking if he appears voluntarily. Ibaneis, a Senate pre-candidate for DF, had previously missed two CPI hearings in December and February.

item.title: Lei cria 474 cargos efetivos na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.374/26, which establishes 474 permanent positions in the Electoral Justice, along with 75 commissioned positions and 245 commissioned functions, to strengthen the security of electronic voting machines and combat fake news in the 2026 elections. The positions will be allocated among the TSE, the TRE-DF, and state TREs, with expenses covered by the courts’ budget allocations.

item.title: Alvo de crítica de Donald Trump, o PIX também já foi condenado por importante economista do PT
item.description: Lula has fiercely defended the PIX, while Donald Trump criticized it, claiming it distorts international trade by affecting the dollar. A prominent PT economist previously condemned the PIX, creating irony given the current government's support. The content is exclusive to subscribers and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Rosamaria Murtinho fala sobre vitalidade aos 93 anos, política e feminismo
item.description: Rosamaria Murtinho, 93, discusses vitality, feminism, vanity and ageism while portraying Iris Apfel in a theater play, mentions her 67-year marriage, states she does not vote for Lula (PT) and advocates for Bolsonaro's (PL) imprisonment, whom she supported in 2018.

item.title: Como a guerra no Irã vai afetar a eleição no Brasil
item.description: The text does not mention any candidates in the Brazilian 2026 presidential election, focusing only on Thomas Traumann's newsletter and a generic note about a possible war in Iran. There is no direct analysis of how the Iran conflict could affect the Brazilian election, only an indirect reference to the topic as a potential agenda. Therefore, it is not possible to identify specific impacts on candidates or electoral campaigns in Brazil.

item.title: Caiado lança candidatura sob a sombra da UDR
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, the PSD's presidential candidate in 2026, launched his campaign emphasizing an uncompromising defense of private property and confrontation with social movements. He is noted as one of the founders of the Democratic Ruralist Union (UDR), created in 1985 as a violent reaction by the agrarian elite to the National Agrarian Reform Plan. Although the PSD was founded with a proposal to be neither right-wing, nor left-wing, nor centrist, the selection of Caiado represents a clear shift toward the far right.

item.title: Moro destaca crescimento do PL no Paraná e contesta debandada de prefeitos
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) emphasized the growth of the PL's state directory in Paraná following his affiliation, stating the party more than doubled in size during the partisan window. He denied reports of a mass exodus of mayors, citing increases in federal and state deputies, and announced Filipe Barros as the new state party president. Moro reiterated his support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential bid, invited new members while excluding petistas and bandidos, and reaffirmed his lead in polls for the Paraná governorship.

item.title: ‘Kkk’ e ‘deboche’: entenda a discussão entre Nikolas e Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro accused Nikolas Ferreira of spreading a right-wing profile that did not support Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, after Nikolas shared content from that profile and replied with 'kkk' to the criticism. Eduardo interpreted the 'kkk' as mockery and responded with a lengthy post accusing Nikolas of disrespect, working against his family, and being corrupted by fame. While allies like Mario Frias and Jair Renan backed Eduardo, Michelle Bolsonaro engaged positively with Nikolas, signaling a deepening rift within the Brazilian right.

item.title: Visando o fim da escala 6×1, Lula busca substituto para Gleisi na articulação política
item.description: President Lula is seeking a replacement for Gleisi Hoffmann in the Ministry of Institutional Relations, prioritizing a political operator with congressional access, possibly a lawmaker, to coordinate government agendas. The appointment is urgent due to the imminent submission of a bill to end the 6×1 work scale and the need to secure Jorge Messias’ nomination to the Supreme Court, both requiring intensive negotiations with congressional leaders. The government plans to wait until after the party window closes to finalize the appointment, avoiding premature decisions.

item.title: Um “termômetro” de votos do Senado sobre a indicação de Messias ao STF
item.description: Federal deputy Gustavo Gayer (PL-GO) launched the 'Votos Senadores' website, which tracks in real time each senator's position on the nomination of Jorge Messias, current Attorney General of the Union, to the Supreme Federal Court (STF). The platform aims to increase political pressure on the Senate vote, functioning as a 'vote thermometer' for Messias' confirmation.
